# pyroid

> Rust ports of the Python libraries used to clean LLM datasets, with the same API and the same output: ftfy, fastText inference, datatrove 0.10.1's quality filters and dedup, Trafilatura 2.3.1 and 1.11.0, rouge-score 0.1.2, sacrebleu 2.6.0, json_repair 0.64.5, datasketch 2.0.0, jieba 0.42.1 and NLTK 3.10.4's tokenizers, plus permissive transliteration. From WARC files, datatrove's FineWeb pipeline runs 8.4x faster with pyroid's steps (104 s vs 871 s, 8 workers, AWS EC2 c7i.4xlarge). Prebuilt wheels for CPython 3.11–3.15 and free-threaded 3.14t/3.15t. pyroid 1.0 is not on PyPI yet; `pip install pyroid` currently gives the unrelated 0.7.x toolkit.

Modules and what they match:

- `pyroid.ftfy` (`import pyroid.ftfy as ftfy`): byte-identical to ftfy 6.3.1.
- `pyroid.fasttext` (`pyroid.fasttext.load_model`): the same .bin/.ftz files, bit-identical predictions per architecture.
- `pyroid.filters`: datatrove's Gopher, C4, FineWeb, PII, C4 bad words, symbol lines and URL filters, with the same decisions.
- `pyroid.dedup`: datatrove's MinHash and sentence dedup, with the same removals.
- `pyroid.trafilatura` (`import pyroid.trafilatura as trafilatura`): the same text as Trafilatura 2.3.1 (the default) or 1.11.0 (`compat="1.11.0"`, the release `datatrove[processing]==0.10.1` installs), byte for byte; `extract_batch(pages, threads=n)` runs pages in parallel; other output formats and metadata are delegated to the installed trafilatura.
- `pyroid.metrics`: ROUGE, BLEU, chrF and chrF++, with scores identical to rouge-score and sacrebleu.
- `pyroid.json_repair`: the same output as json_repair, in linear time.
- `pyroid.datasketch`: datasketch 2.0.0's MinHash, LeanMinHash and LSH indexes with the same hash values and query results; needs numpy.
- `pyroid.jieba` (`import pyroid.jieba as jieba`): the same words, offsets and frequencies as jieba 0.42.1, with the default dictionary built in; `lcut(docs, threads=n)` segments a batch in parallel.
- `pyroid.nltk` (`import pyroid.nltk as nltk`): the same sentences, tokens and offsets as NLTK 3.10.4's `sent_tokenize` (Punkt, with the user's installed `punkt_tab` models), `word_tokenize`, Treebank tokenizers and detokenizer, and regexp tokenizers for common patterns; `sent_tokenize(docs, threads=n)` and `word_tokenize(docs, threads=n)` run a batch in parallel; `pyroid.patch("nltk")` swaps them into an installed NLTK.
- `pyroid.translit`: `anyascii()` byte-identical to anyascii 0.3.3; `unidecode()` with Unidecode's signature and errors= semantics but anyascii's output.

Integrations: the `pyroid clean IN OUT --recipe fineweb` command line (many files, `--workers`, `--shard I/N`, s3:// gs:// hf:// inputs, resumable runs, `pyroid dedup signatures|buckets|cluster|filter` for MinHash across shards), `pyroid.patch("ftfy", "fasttext")` for code you don't own (also `anyascii`, `datasketch`, `trafilatura`, `nltk`), datatrove drop-in steps (`pyroid.integrations.datatrove`, `Trafilatura` included; it has no 1 s timeout, so results do not vary between runs) and Hugging Face `datasets` helpers (`pyroid.integrations.hf`). There are no runtime dependencies; the extras are `[fasttext]` (numpy), `[cli]` (pyarrow), `[datatrove]` and `[hf]`.

Conventions shared by every module:

- Batch functions take a `str`, a `list`/`tuple` of `str`, or an Arrow string column (pyarrow, polars, pandas, HF datasets). Text and masks come back in the same kind (Arrow input gives a `pyroid.Column`, which converts with `pyarrow.chunked_array(col)` or `polars.Series(col)`); `fasttext.Model.predict` on a batch returns lists, and `get_sentence_vector` numpy arrays.
- Transforms return text (unchanged documents are the original objects); predicates return a keep mask (`list[bool]` for a list), never a filtered list.
- `threads=None` uses all cores, `threads=n` at most n, `threads=1` the calling thread. Batches release the GIL; free-threaded builds stay GIL-free.
- Where a module meets an option or input it does not port, it delegates to the real library and emits `pyroid.FallbackWarning` (or raises `pyroid.PyroidError` if that library is missing): some ftfy functions and options, metrics tokenizers such as ja-mecab, json_repair's `schema=`, and the filters' and MinHash's `python_tokenizer=True` path for languages pyroid does not tokenize natively (330 of datatrove's 4,343 codes, e.g. Vietnamese and Thai; and the 4 Japanese codes unless a SudachiDict dictionary is installed with `pip install sudachidict-core`). Otherwise modules raise rather than approximate. Errors: `pyroid.InputError` is a `TypeError`.
- To clean many documents with ftfy, prefer `pyroid.ftfy.fix_text_batch(docs)` over a loop of `fix_text`. To run several datatrove filters, use `pyroid.filters.apply(docs, [GopherRepetition(), GopherQuality(), C4Quality(...), FineWebQuality()])`, which returns `FilterResult(keep, reason, text)`. For many ROUGE pairs use `RougeScorer.score_batch`; for many JSON documents `pyroid.json_repair.repair_json_batch`.

## Docs

- [Home](https://ao.github.io/pyroid/): what pyroid is, the two zero-code entry points, the 30-second example
- [Install](https://ao.github.io/pyroid/install/): extras, wheels and platforms
- [Inputs and outputs](https://ao.github.io/pyroid/concepts/inputs/): str/list/tuple/Arrow in, the same kind out; masks; nulls
- [Threads and free-threading](https://ao.github.io/pyroid/concepts/threads/): `threads=`, the GIL, 3.14t/3.15t
- [Fallbacks](https://ao.github.io/pyroid/concepts/fallbacks/): `pyroid.FallbackWarning`, `python_tokenizer=True`
- [Errors](https://ao.github.io/pyroid/concepts/errors/): exception types

## Guides

- [pyroid.ftfy](https://ao.github.io/pyroid/guides/ftfy/): drop-in ftfy 6.3.1, `fix_text_batch`, differences from ftfy
- [pyroid.fasttext](https://ao.github.io/pyroid/guides/fasttext/): fastText inference, batches, threads, differences from fastText
- [pyroid.filters](https://ao.github.io/pyroid/guides/filters/): datatrove's Gopher, C4, FineWeb, PII, bad-words, symbol-lines and URL filters, `apply`, differences from datatrove
- [pyroid.dedup](https://ao.github.io/pyroid/guides/dedup/): datatrove-identical MinHash dedup, sentence dedup and exact dedup
- [pyroid.translit](https://ao.github.io/pyroid/guides/translit/): anyascii-identical transliteration with Unidecode's signature (output is not Unidecode's)
- [pyroid.metrics](https://ao.github.io/pyroid/guides/metrics/): drop-in rouge-score and sacrebleu (BLEU, chrF), batch scoring, differences
- [pyroid.json_repair](https://ao.github.io/pyroid/guides/json_repair/): drop-in json_repair, `repair_json_batch`, differences from json_repair
- [pyroid.datasketch](https://ao.github.io/pyroid/guides/datasketch/): drop-in datasketch 2.0.0 (MinHash, LeanMinHash, MinHashLSH, LSH Forest, LSH Ensemble), `minhash_batch`, differences from datasketch
- [pyroid.jieba](https://ao.github.io/pyroid/guides/jieba/): drop-in jieba 0.42.1, batches, user dictionaries, differences from jieba
- [pyroid.trafilatura](https://ao.github.io/pyroid/guides/trafilatura/): drop-in Trafilatura 2.3.1 and 1.11.0, how to choose a mode, `extract_batch`, the datatrove step, differences
- [pyroid.nltk](https://ao.github.io/pyroid/guides/nltk/): drop-in NLTK 3.10.4 Punkt, Treebank and regexp tokenizers, punkt_tab models, differences from NLTK
- [Languages](https://ao.github.io/pyroid/guides/languages/): which datatrove language codes are native, which need `python_tokenizer=True`, how to choose

## Integrations

- [The pyroid command line](https://ao.github.io/pyroid/guides/cli/): `pyroid clean`, `langid`, `dedup`, `translit`, `run`; every option
- [Large datasets](https://ao.github.io/pyroid/guides/large-datasets/): thousands of files, `--workers`, `--shard`, remote inputs, resuming, MinHash dedup across shards
- [pyroid.patch()](https://ao.github.io/pyroid/guides/patch/): redirect `import ftfy`, `fasttext`, `anyascii`, `datasketch`, `trafilatura` or `nltk` to pyroid in code you don't own
- [datatrove steps](https://ao.github.io/pyroid/guides/datatrove/): drop-in datatrove pipeline steps with the same names and signatures
- [Hugging Face datasets](https://ao.github.io/pyroid/guides/huggingface/): batched callables for `Dataset.map`/`filter`, the FineWeb recipe
